summary.text: Hank Johnson is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 4th Congressional District, serving since 2007 and elected to his 10th term in 2024. A lawyer who practiced in Decatur and served as a magistrate judge and DeKalb County Commissioner before Congress, he sits on the House Judiciary Committee. He is seeking re-election.

paragraphs.text: Graduated from Clark College (now Clark Atlanta University) in 1976 with a B.A. in political science and from Texas Southern University's Thurgood Marshall School of Law in 1979.
According to his official biography, practiced law for 27 years in Decatur, Georgia, specializing in criminal defense, civil rights, and personal injury law (Ballotpedia says more than 25 years).
According to his official biography, served as a magistrate judge for 12 years.
Served as a DeKalb County Commissioner, five years according to his official biography (Ballotpedia lists 2000 to 2005), including as chair of the county's budget committee from 2002 to 2005.
Challenged Rep. Cynthia McKinney in the 2006 Democratic primary, forced a runoff, and won the August 8, 2006 runoff with about 59% of the vote; he took office in January 2007.

Serves on the House Judiciary Committee, where he is ranking member of the Subcommittee on Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet, and on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee (2025-2026).

According to his official biography, in 2010 he was a member of the House prosecution team in the impeachment trial of Judge G. Thomas Porteous Jr., and he introduced the FAIR Act on forced arbitration, which passed the House twice, and the Stop Militarizing Law Enforcement Act.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, DeKalb County Commissioner Mereda Davis Johnson, have two adult children.
